seaa-cross-country-champs-stanmer-park-b: High drama on the South Downs Top: Phil Wicks is in full flight - half distance and he's 30 metres clear of the field. Pictures by Steve Wicks. Alan Mead writes:- When past cross country champion Gerry North was asked what he thought of the Stanmer Park course he opined … “this is a tough one!” … and surveying the rolling hills of the South Downs one couldn’t help agreeing with him. The going was firm but the there was nary a level stretch anywhere … and of course it was 15 kilometres in length. Desperate for a race after missing planned outings for various reasons and slightly uneasy about a hip niggle, Phil Wicks made a decision to run on the morning of the race. The ubiquitous Cockerpillar was there, James Kelly wouldn’t miss the ‘Southern’ for all the sunshine in Madrid (although his Spanish club mates could not quite comprehend a 2,000 mile round trip to compete over 15k of English style cross country) and as start time neared Lander Eguia and Mike Trees both arrived, nursing colds but thinking that they must turn out to ensure we had a full squad. Sadly their efforts only saw our numbers reach five, one short of the team requirement. After the charge along the start stretch the first turn saw Phil Wicks in the front rank and as the initial small lap (itself containing a substantial climb) was completed and the field headed out into Downs proper, all the leading contenders were in place. Slowly the protagonists were whittled down and at 6k three men were clear of the field: Neilsen Hall (Bedford &C), Glen Watts (Shaftesbury Barnet) and Phil tucked in behind about two metres back but picking up that small deficit as they disappeared from view onto the second large loop. A substantial crowd of fans had climbed to a vantage point to see the runners twice on each circuit and they eagerly scanned the track ahead, waiting for the runners to emerge from woodland … “here they come,” … and “Wicks” was the name on the lips of the cognoscenti. He was 30 metres clear of the other two … and going away! Sure enough that lead did grow … 40 metres … some say it was more. In the minds of all, Phil was heading for a third win in this championship to add to his victories of 2007 (Holkham Hall, Norfolk) and 2009 (Hillingdon House Farm, Uxbridge). One couldn’t entirely disregard the opposition for those splintered chasers had slowly coalesced into a pursuing bunch of five as the last lap was begun … but no, the gap was too big now. Down to the finish stretch, then, and wait for the arrival … and after what seemed like an interminable interlude, there he was in the distance bursting out of the coppice at the top of the hill, perhaps 500 metres to go and heading down the steep slope towards the final turn; but … gasp! … there also was Ben Tickner, 20m behind and using that last drop like a fell runner. One could see the gap diminishing; was Phil was aware of the danger? Such was Tickner’s momentum that he was on the Belgravian as the turn was made into the finish stretch and no amount of gear changing by our man could match his rival's pace. While the winner celebrated as he crossed the line, tugging at his vest to give prominence to the ‘Wells City’ logo, an already disconsolate Phil Wicks maintained his pace to take the silver medal. Phil was fuming at the way things had turned out. “I can accept being beaten on any day of the week,” he later pronounced, “but to lose like that is hard to take. I won’t forget that for a while.” Nevertheless, it was a superb run from a man not yet at the top of his game and whatever he thought, the general opinion was: “Wicksy’s back!” James Kelly cannot be praised highly enough for his battling run in the twenties, finishing in 16th and up eleven spots on last year. His stress fracture now seems to be a thing of the past (touch wood) and he is planning another crack at the London Marathon. womens-surrey-cross-country-league-divis: Famous Five Save The Day Will Cockerell writes:- Enid Blyton could've scripted the Belles here. A quaint village scene with a picturesque blanket of snow, but underneath the idyllic veneer, lurked menace, trouble and danger! The only way promotion could elude us was if we fielded two short of a full team, and we cut it very fine with a huge injured and unavailable list - 26 of 'em. Make that 27 when Maureen had 'a touch of the Nellies' to her train-catching strategy, and took one bound for Reading not Woking. Bad idea, and now we were down to the bare 5... Vicki flew in to Heathrow without alarm, using the race as a warm-up to Sunday's Bramley 20, and Fee drove down the night before and although her lad locked the car keys in the boot, this only incapacitated the vehicle, but not mama; nice try though. Hester's little boy picked up the winter vomiting bug, but she tore herself from his bedside with wonderful club spirit. Late on Friday, the TM was fearing such low numbers he had a panicky howl on email, and the SOS cry shook loose a couple of good apples in Catriona and Rieko. To the start then and with a bottleneck 150 yards hence, Charlie Dickinson advised a chipper start, and boy did they. Fee was inside the top dozen overall and Hester and Rieko went out very quickly - but they're getting fit these two, and at half-way were still devouring bodies. Vicki kept watch, sticking out as the track runner amongst the 'grinders', while Catriona paid a small price for her early fireworks but was providing a solid anchor. Lap two and under instructions should any ankles be broken, to crawl over broken glass to the finish, Fee completed another resounding race, just a few seconds down on fourth - to leapfrog to the top of the Cross-country plate table in the process. Rieko finally shook off the attentions of Hester, with both girls producing their finest runs for Belgrave, and Vicki and Cat smoothly saw us home. So we're up then - as Div 2 champions - but if not for one or two of this Famous Five it could have been a ghastly cock-up. THH looked awesome to take Div 1, but we're not scared and will seek to hit them hard in eight months time. Thanks to all who competed in what has been a really fun and entertaining league campaign. mens-ecca-english-cc-champs-parliament-h: A new name on the 'Parker Bowl' Alan Mead writes :- One hundred and twenty five National Cross Country races have now taken place and this latest edition, held on a balmy spring-like day, was a classic as the perhaps overlooked Keith Gerrard of Newham & Essex Beagles proved unbeatable. It wasn’t a bad day for the Bels as we turned out ten men and reminded ourselves that tucked away among our non-runners was an entered sextet that could have given team winners Leeds City a run for their money had they been in good 'nick' or otherwise available. Still, it’s not about those one enters but those who actually run and we had to settle for a final team spot of 25th. It’s been far worse than that. Yet another super run came from James Kelly (who, nevertheless, was hoping for something a little higher) and thus a new name goes onto the ‘Parker Bowl’ awarded to the first Belgravian to finish. Good to see Tom Hadfield and Kevin Gadd turning out – their first outings this winter! Always enjoying his racing, Malik Nehaily was pleased to hear his name being called out by our men’s team as they paused in their preparations to give him a shout as he passed the flag. womens-ecca-english-cc-champs-parliament: Assault on Top 10 a No, but not a Never Will Cockerell writes :- Whereas all our Christmases came at once at the Southern, with a dream team and a freak mathematical parlay giving us that epic bronze, we had to get our heads down and grind out respectability here. Out of 22 entered runners we had every hope of fielding at least a dozen starters here and a top 8 place, but our injury list is still pushing on for double figures, several key personnel were away, and Smurph made the long journey down from Cheshire, but alas she couldn't fool nature and was unable to shake off the remnants of flu. However, it was still seven eager Belles on hand to enjoy the Heath at it most glorious - and benign - and a huge field of 650. Ten years on from the 'Apocalypse Now' that was Bristol and Anne Hegvold's epic 32nd, where she was our only finisher, she was back anchoring us here, with a clinical run. Tilly was on hand to play yet another perfect piece of middle-order steadiness, running most of the first 10 minutes with Anne, before slowly drifting up through the pack. It was great to welcome MGS back into the fold - a difficult chick to pin down since making her club debut in the pressure cauldron that was Milton Keynes last year. But what a welcome she gave us, cresting the beastly initial climb inside the top 50. A tad frisky perhaps, but this ultra-marathoner wasn't going to buckle too badly over a trifling 8k, and kept a resounding run from Fee in sight. Fee was hotter here than at the Southern, and after a cautious start was bearing down on the top 100 by the end, to sign her off her magnificent debut XC season for the Belles with a flourish. With expert back-up from Hester, Rieko and Maureen, we had found our level, sweet 16th. Yes, we craved more a fortnight ago but just look at the calibre who couldn't help us here: Amend, Blizzard, Bryson, Cole, Dagne, Murphy, Quispel, Smith - at least four of those have donned the England vest, and we have high hopes that we shall be benefitting from many of them when we hit the roads of Milton Keynes, Sutton Park and of course the London Marathon in the weeks to come. A text later from Mary Grace summed up the mood of this happy tribe: "Super experience! Definite 2013 mgx". Good running came from Alice Harray, still eleven years old but nevertheless beating over one third of the Under 13 Girls' field. cau-inter-counties-cc-championship-cofto: Wicks third in Inter-Counties Underlining yet again that everything seems to be falling into place as he works towards his Spring-time and Summer goals, Phil Wicks, coached by Matt Whiting, took some great scalps as he ran to third place in the Inter-Counties Cross Country Championship. On the second lap of the rolling hills of Cofton Park Phil and Jonny Hay were a little detached from the leaders in 6th and 7th. Lap three saw a strong push from National Champion Keith Gerrard and he built on this to earn another fine win. Meanwhile, our man was also pulling back rivals ... Brownlee ... Taylor ... and as the finish neared there was a possibility that he might even take the silver medal but Ricky Stevenson had too much pace. seaa-mens-12-stage-road-relay-stantonbur: Boldly going to the final frontier “It’s Milton Keynes, Captain, but not as we know it.” With the expense of hiring the Open University facilities going up like the Starship Enterprise, writes Alan Mead , the organisers switched venue to the track at Stantonbury Stadium, trekking a few miles even further up the road and boldly going to the northern-most frontier of the South of England. It’s the sort of thing that ‘stattos’ hate: their carefully built up facts and figures are consigned to history while a new batch has to be begun. But one has to say that the stadium was a good location – although the markings out on the course for the long stage might have to be thought through a bit more. Yes, long stage men “keep left” – but only at the end of the first lap. One poor soul went round three times and another (difficult to believe this) set out on a fourth lap of Linford Wood before someone put him out of his misery. Not as we know it, either, as for the first time in over a decade we were not expecting to get into the medals – a feat that only eluded us once on the old circuit. With quite a few of the stellar team preoccupied with other goals our aim was a comfortable qualification for the National. With a little less expectation comes a little less pressure – and you know what? It was a nice relaxed afternoon – once everyone was there. Andrew Connick made his debut in the ‘A’ team but would have much preferred a short stage. Obliging character that he is, however, he set out on the initial long leg with his nose just showing ahead in the front rank as forty plus teams set out through the gates. He was kicking himself later, feeling that he hadn’t done himself justice, but he did set things up perfectly for Steve Davies who ripped up the red paths and took the team up 18 places to 3rd; surely this would be best time of the day. Surrey League stalwarts the Cockerpillar and Wardy kept us in 8th and then James Fairbourn found himself touring MK on an ‘A’ team long stage when only a week or so earlier he’d said: “I’ve started training again so put me down for a short one in the ‘B’ team.” In good nick, ‘Sharpy’ set sixth best time of the day for his 5k stint and we followed up with Paskar whose elegant and flowing running style drew admiration as he set out – and even more when he got back having clocked a mere 23:35 for one of the day’s best times. We were in fourth! Exactly as planned and now, would the gaps have grown sufficiently to allow us to retain a reasonable finishing position? Yes indeed. A lean looking but short-on-training Sp8y lost only one spot as he ran some 45 seconds slower than he’ll be aiming for at Sutton Park; and then Mal, Stuart, Lander and Mike clung on so well for our hoped for place in the top ten. Good work! For much of the time Kent AC had been beavering away at the head of affairs but were under attack from Highgate near the end, with both teams being swept up by the Beagles who had been languishing behind the Bels until stage seven. seaa-womens-6-stage-road-relay-stantonbu: A Great Warrior Returns Will Cockerell writes:- It was gently pointed out to the TM during the race that no-one from 2011's mini dream-team returned to the fray, and indeed four of them have missed the entire season! The absences are just a reflection of what a tough sport this is and how fickle the running gods can be. All of the 2011 six remain valuable Belgravians, but two are out with long-term injury, two more ran cracking 10k's elsewhere, Miss Cole was on classy duathlon duty and Lenka writes from Prague to say she loved racing for us and hopes to again in the coming years. So... all change, and in a race of sound standard, we were given a good start by Fee whose time, perhaps surprisingly, stood up to be our fastest of the day. Nelle travelled for many hours to be there, and ground out a net return of plus 1. There's more to come in her tank and it'll arrive soon enough. The Queen is back, long live the Queen. Our National cross-country champion from 2004 hasn't raced since the Birmingham half-marathon of October 2008. Birhan has had another child and knee surgery since then, and it was great to see her back in the claret and gold. She really wanted to pull out in the days leading up to the race as she fought a bad tooth infection, but realized that to get back racing, you've gotta' get back racing. It was painful and her time had her wincing as much as her tooth, but the stride is still unmistakably classy and at just 33 there's still time for Birhan to return to a high standard. Anne ran well and looked good with some big triathlons all over the world to anticipate in the coming months; and Vicki was a revelation, with her best run of the season, and a tempo 21-miler in her legs from the day before. Rieko arrived a full 27 minutes before her leg which is about five times earlier than normal, to anchor us home yet again, and only leak a single position. So 12th it is, missing several fantastic runners, nearly all of whom are sharpening their talons with SP in mind. And with a marathon squad sent straight from the angels, our season could yet end with a couple of big bangs. 1 Aldershot F&D 1:44:17; 2 Aldershot F&D 'B' 1:50:23; 3 Dulwich R 1:53:02; 4 Windsor SEH 1:54:08; 5 Woodford Green wEL 1:54:10... 12 Belgrave H 2:00:31. 33 teams started, 27 finished. erra-national-mens-12-stage-road-relay-s: An epic chase in Sutton Park All things considered one would have to say that it was a successful day, writes Alan Mead . We were just one runner away from the medals and two runners away from the win. Yes, most clubs can point to those who they were unable to include in their line-up, but sometimes the stars in the athletic firmament do all fall into a winning conjunction … and we have those stars. There are more medals to come for the Bels. The news the evening before the race that an unwell Cockerpillar would probably not be able to run meant that reserve Martin Holm had to be called up ‘just in case’ and the ever-obliging Andrew Connick had to move to a ‘long-un’ … again. Then, at sparrow-chirp on race-day, as three Belgravians belying the 220 years that they shared between them erected the tent, further news came in that they did not want to hear: the Sharpster’s inflamed Achilles tendon would not take the strain of a long stage but he’d be alright on a short one. For the first two, the anticipated ‘run-off’ during warm up to decide which of them would tackle the now vacant long stage, proved to be unnecessary as the ‘pillar took a turn around a motorway service station to see how he felt … and it wasn’t good. So at 12 noon Martin Holm was plunged into the first stage cauldron with instructions from everyone ringing in his ears … “just run your own race.” It was tough for MBH as he unexpectedly faced many of the UK’s finest road runners but he plugged away well and set things up for what had always been planned as a chasing game; and what an epic chase it was. Stephen grabbed 16 places back on stage two and Andrew Connick – a 1:51 800 man – came forward again over the 5 miles plus of the long leg and became more pleased with his time as the day wore on and other long-stagers came up some way short of their expectations. Probably the highlight of the day was to see Nick Goolab on the road again after what Her Majesty would describe as an annus horribilis. Didn’t he just look the business as he glided up the final 300 metres, taking us up to 22nd? Welcome back Nick! All set for a tilt at 2:18 in the following week’s London Marathon, James Kelly felt good and looked great as he toured Sutton Park – but was surprised to find that all this good feeling didn’t lead to anything faster than a run eight seconds short of his 2009 pb. There’s no doubting his strength though, as recent back to back 68 minute half marathons have shown; we wish him luck for his 26.2 target. Now living in Spain and working in Gibraltar, a far from his best JB was a minute and a three-quarters slower than his best for the short stage but he held the team steady in 20th as the race reached half way. Painful though his run no doubt was, a visit to Sutton Park was working its magic and he later vowed to return in better shape for the next one. An already cool and breezy day seemed to take a chillier turn as the race progressed. The winning 26:01 on stage one, somewhat slower than is normally returned on the opening leg, was still standing up as the day’s best. Five different teams had taken their turn at the head of the field but Tipton Harriers were staking a strong claim as we rolled Russell into the fray … and that long-stage hoodoo mystified another Belgravian. Surely a 26-something would come from R D-C but, no, his 27:21 was exactly one minute slower than his 2009 clocking in spite of being eighth best on his stage. We were into the ‘teens’ though as Sp8y took charge and as good as his word he was ’45 seconds faster than at Milton Keynes,’ as he moved up three more to send out twenty-three year-old Michael Mulhare. Now we did see a sub-27 on the watch as Michael took us past Woodford, Highgate and Shettlestone into 10th. A betting man might well put something on a sub-26 from this man at some time in the not-too-distant future. The gaps were large and Captain Wardy, head full of cold, didn’t see a soul on his short stage but moved up a place as Bristol & West ran out of men. His 15:30 for 9th best pretty much matched Sp8y’s 15:29 and their challenge as to who would be fastest come the National was accepted as draw. He tells us that this was his last relay – we can’t believe that! Tipton were now sure to be winners and Leeds the likely silver medallists but the rumours were that Birchfield would not be able to hold on to the bronze medal position … and they didn’t as one of their men now went 30:00 plus on stage eleven and Notts AC came through. Large gaps or not, Paskar was intent on doing something special and we were a very respectable 7th by the time he’d disposed of Bedford & County and the Scottish club Central running to our best long stage time of the day – 26:42 – and fastest for his leg. Now it was all up to Steve Davies. At team selection time we’d hoped he’d be able to run us into the medals but although we hadn’t been able to place him in that position, he turned on another stage best and took us past Aldershot & Farnham to 6th and second best Southern club behind the Beagles who were 5th. It was a superb run from Steve who was 9th best on the day and although 8 seconds shy of his fastest, bearing in mind the conditions and the late leg, surely he'd just given us his best ever run on the circuit. british-athletics-league-national-divisi: Above: The sprint dudes clocked 41.71 - Wade Bennett-Jackson, Greg Cackett, Seun Marcus and Thom Evans . Below Right: Ciaran Collins set a 400m pb of 49.74. Below left Paskar Owor and Á lberto Lozano de Pedro were a formidable pairing in the middle distance races. Pictures by Bill Laws. Room for improvement Man on a mission Having missed most of last season Mark Allen is a man on a mission. His aim by the end of the summer is to climb to seventh spot on the Belgrave all time BAL points list.* The ex-decathlete arrived at Lee Valley ready for a challenge. And he got it. He opened with the hammer at 11.30am, filled a high jump gap at 12.30 and simultaneously competed in the javelin and shot at 3.05pm. He also wanted to compete in the discus at 1.00pm but veterans Abi Ekoku and Leith Marar (both long time big point earners for Belgrave) thwarted him. But the throws proved problematic. First John Osazuwa had two no throws in the hammer and his final safe effort was some 20m short of his pb so Mark made the cut and John didn’t. And then Abi Ekoku had two no throws in the discus and his safe final effort was more than 20m shy of his pb. Aaron Crawford gained good points in a high standard javelin competition but overall the throws squad didn’t quite fulfil its promise. While we were at least filling the field events once again there were big gaps on the track. With only J C Roghi in the 400H’s and Paskar Owor in the 800’s we gleaned just 12 points from the 56 on offer. But worse was to come as we had nobody in the chase. So effectively we had scored just 12 points from 84. But there was better news on the way thanks to our speed men. Stunning time The first glimpse of hope came in the n/s 100m where Seun Marcus, Pierre Walker and new man Thom Evans all ran pb’s. Add to them last year’s UK Challenge winner Greg Cackett and Wade Bennett Jackson (who missed the last two seasons through injury) and suddenly we had hope; and we were not disappointed. First Greg ripped to victory in the 100A in a fine pb of 10.43sec then to be followed by Wade with another win in the 100B producing an equally stunning time of 10.49sec. That will make a few people sit up as many had written Wade off. The sprint relay later in the match was eagerly awaited and provided another win for out sprinters. So, we'd taken a total of 72 points from the 72 on offer. With so many good sprinters on show these really were exceptional results. And our other speed men were also enjoying themselves. The 110H proved an exceptional race with WSEH’s Lawrence Clarke speeding to a legal 13.47sec victory which shattered the Divisional record held by our own William Sharman (13.8 in 2009). Ex triple jumper Gary Wilson produced a 14.87sec pb for a Belgrave third spot and with JC in 5th place in the 110HB race we had gleaned more good points. Yet another pb was to follow. New member Ciaran Collins reduced his to 49.74sec gaining a valuable sixth place in the 400A. Meanwhile the jumpers were toiling away in temperatures pushing 27deg C. Daniel Gardner won the A PV in an outdoor pb of 4.90m ably backed by Cameron Johnson who placed 4th in the B pool. Paul Ogun was jumping big but unfortunately was also destroying the plasticine on the long jump board. Two no jumps meant a safe third attempt which was not good enough to make the cut. As recompense Paul triple jumped. David Wellstead backed up both events but was disappointed with below par jumps. Back on the track Wade Bennett-Jackson led the 200A up to 190m but faded badly to get useful third place points. Still, he is racing himself to fitness and there will be big improvements to come. He even volunteered for a leg in the 400 relay. First appearance The 1500m saw the first appearance for Belgrave of Álberto Lozano de Pedro. With A and B strings running together the first man home for each team scores in the A event and the second man in the B. More of a cross and road man Alberto sat at the back and when Paskar made a move on the leaders Álberto too made his move. Paskar was rewarded with second in the A race and Álberto concluded a fine début for Belgrave with a win in the B race. Twenty minutes later both men lined up for the 5000m. Paskar had the luxury of watching Álberto move from 10th to 2nd place on lap 10 with what can only be described as a 150m sprint. He then sat on Cardiff’s up and coming Rowan Axe before unleashing a ferocious kick to gain his first A string points for the club. Meanwhile Paskar cruised in for a B string win and maximum points. Last year the final meeting event – the 4 x 400 relay – proved a step too far. This year we had numbers to compete. Junior Vladimir Woodham-Smith got pushed around a bit at the second take over and suffered accordingly but a fine final leg by Melvyn Anukam gained 6th spot and 6 valuable points. So after a day of downs and ups the team had clawed itself up to equal fifth spot, just 6 points off third place. It was that close. The next match is at Gateshead on the 30th June. The big question is can we get a full squad out for that one? aviva-uka-championships-olympic-trials-b: Another UKA title for Goldie Sayers The final day of the UKA Championships & Olympic Trials saw two more titles fall to Belgravians and hopefully further places booked for the Olympic Team. An amazing tenth consecutive senior national javelin title went to Goldie Sayers - who was just out of the medals in fourth place at the Beijing Olympics where she threw her best ever distance (and British Record) of 65.75 metres. With a 64.73 in the Samsung Diamond League in Rome earlier this season she's not so far behind the sort of distance that could see a medal come her way in London. It would be Goldie's third Olympic Games. Video interview with Goldie Will Sharman was unlucky to place 4th in a very tight sprint hurdles final and Samson Oni - who has the Olympic Standard height of 2.31 tucked away from January this year - placed second in the high jump and will surely be a part of the Olympic team. Full results | Belgrave results Pressured Chambers storms to a dramatic win After well publicised years in the wilderness and at last gaining at least the legal possibility of competing in the 2012 Olympic Games the now 34 year-old Dwain Chambers had to face perhaps his toughest ever domestic 100 metre field, loaded with up and coming youngsters, some nearly half his age. The pressure was immense ... as can be seen by Dwain's reaction after he crossed the line ... but the win was his in 10.25 secs. It still remains for the Belgrave man to find the qualifying time of 10.18 and hopefully he can achieve this at the European Championships which start in Helsinki this week. BBC Video Also in the 100 metres the ever consistent Greg Cackett was just 100th of a second from his best ever time in winning his heat in 10.44 but was unable to get through the semi-final stage. Getenesh Tamirat ran to 4th in the women's 10,000 metres with a time of 33:09.47 and she was the second UK runner (although there were only four UK participants). Jodie Favell set a personal record in her heat of the 400 metre hurdles. Steve Davies made the final of the 1500 metres but was unable to improve on the 3:46.72 from his heat. british-athletics-league-national-divisi: It's hard graft in windy Gateshead The Weather The Thursday before the match saw the Gateshead area struck by storms so severe that seasoned travellers reported conditions worse than the most severe tropical downpours. TV news showed pictures of the Tyne Bridge being struck by lightning and cars submerged under four feet of water. As the team headed towards Newcastle it was not known whether the match would proceed. Game on Last year thirteen brave souls journeyed to Gateshead. This year an expanded team of sixteen took to the stage. With no specialist vaulters or high jumpers and Paul Ogun and David Wellstead doubling the long and triple it was left to Mark Allen and Andy Boudrie to step in and harvest a few precious points in the vertical jumps. The throws squad was also reduced in numbers with Mark Allen, Matt Richards and Aaron Crawford covering the four throws. Matt has been injured since May and was delighted with a second placing in the hammer in his first outing of the season. Head winds gusting The track started with the sprinters suffering from head winds gusting up to 5m/s. With no chance of good times it was a case of chasing points. Greg Cackett raced to a clear win in the A100. Wade Bennett Jackson couldn’t repeat his match 1 win in the B100 and settled for silver. Clearly he was struggling and it turned out he hadn’t trained since the previous weeks Olympic trials and was carrying a hamstring niggle. This showed in the A200 where he finished fourth and nearly scuppered the sprint relay as he struggled on the first leg. Fortunately Greg Cackett put the brakes on and, unlike the UK’s men’s squad at the Euro Champs, the baton passed safely to finish in third thanks to Greg, Cameron Webb and a storming home straight by sprint hurdler Gary Wilson. Late surge The track events contributed the majority of the points thanks to fine 400’s from new member Andrew Boudrie and Ciaran Collins. Steve Davies added strength winning the A 800 and A1500. The latter race saw an epic lead out by TVH’s Darren Hall who gave 100% but still couldn’t resist the late surge of Steve closely followed by Paskar Owor who won the B event. Paskar gained more valuable in the 3000 backed by Will Cockerell who had travelled up on the day to be our first steeplechaser to toe the start line this season. It was pleasing to see JC run a season’s best in the 400H in windy conditions. Hero of the day - Mark Allen So, once again a small team mixed and matched to gain every point. Hero of the day was Mark Allen who managed six events (The League limit is seven so there is room for improvement!). The point spread between teams is closer than ever this year and just a few extra athletes would have made a huge difference. We seem to have said that after the first match. uk-womens-athletics-league-division-thre: Great work by the Belles in Liverpool Taking a team to the further flung reaches of the country is always problematic and with Team Manager Bob Bridges temporarily out of action Don Anderson stepped up to drive the majority of our squad in a minibus from Battersea to Liverpool on the morning of the match. A hold up on the M1 meant a late arrival but thankfully the organisers agreed to hold back the timetable half an hour and as our girls arrived they swung straight into action. With Don switching into timekeeper mode, Val offering her services as a track judge and Rex Bale, Jack Albrow and Mike Causer doing duty on the field we even earned a full score for our officials. Big thanks to them. A mazing stuff As the early results came in, with a great start in the 400m hurdles thanks to Louise Aylwin and Ashleigh Horrobin, soon the team were in third team spot ... and then third became second when we picked up two third spots in the 100m ... amazing stuff ... although Tamara Hamond was not impressed with her sprint performances and later put herself forward to run the 2k steeplechase as penance! It was wonderful to have Lou Blizzard and Sarah Murphy back in the team; both are now resident in the North and they boosted our middle-distance scores handsomely. Awesome As usual heptathlete Jodie Favell was everywhere. She normally manages at least one win and here it came in the long jump, and with Michelle Nestor taking second in the 'B' this became a high scoring event for us. Rebecca Pile was awesome in winning the 400 metres and followed up with a 200m 'B' win and last leg in the long relay. Delighted Vilma Thompson, Hazel Mead and sprinter Haylene Ryan made sure that all throwing events were covered and the only discipline not tackled by a Belgravian was the pole vault. Gradually, as the match drew to a conclusion and things levelled out the Belles were delighted with a final team place of fourth ... which takes them up to equal fourth in the division. Time to catch breath ... before the long haul home again! british-athletics-league-national-divisi: Chasing every extra point Full results | Photos by Emanuelis Stasaitis Match 3 provided a nostalgic chance to see the tired Copthall stadium for the last time. Building works behind the back straight have already started as part of a massive £20million re-build following the sale of the site to Saracens rugby club. Shaftesbury Barnet have negotiated a 30 year lease so athletics will be retained in the forseeable future thanks to an innovative design including retractable seating which will cover the ends of the track through the rugby season. Ground works meant that several events had to be held outside the track and your elderly team manager's fitness was tested as he scurried from event to event. Transport delays But this was not the only challenge. This match coincided with the Olympic road race which had closed many roads in Surrey and South London. The inevitable transport delays and the 11.00am start to this double fixture were bound to throw up problems. David Wellstead missed the 11.00 am long jump start and arrived just in time to record a modest third round effort. But Paul Ogun went some way to compensate by winning the A event with his last jump. Later in the triple jump both men responded well and David produced a season's best to get second spot in the B competition with Paul third in the A event. Alongside them in the pole vault junior Daniel Gardner won with a new pb of 5.10m and Andy Boudrie popped over a height for B points. Andy too had been delayed and missed the high jump where our sole competitor was Mark Allen. Mark buzzed from event to event gaining valuable points. In the 11.00am hammer he led specialist Matt Richards until the last round when Matt finally composed himself and powered out a winning effort just shy of 60m. With Mark winning the B we had maximum points in the hammer. The discus also produced good points with Leith Marar fourth in the A and again Mark winning the B. But the javelin suffered from the loss of Aaron Crawford while the shot yielded meagre points. Peter Mayfield responded to a last minute call and gained valuable points in the javelin and shot to back up Mark Allen. Exciting races and times The track produced some exciting races and times. But our early week hopes of a track points bonanza suffered a blow when on Friday night Wade Bennett Jackson reported unfit. On the day Pierre Walker stepped into the B100 and Cameron Webb the B200 both acquitting themselves well and gleaning more points. Greg Cackett saved the day by doubling the 100 and 200 finishing a close second in each high quality sprint. Interestingly the Division 1 sprints were faster than the Premiership ones which followed in this double match fixture. The middle distance races proved compelling with several men competing in the team for the first time this year. It was great to see Kris Gauson back. He has been in the States for four years and after a long collegiate season had already brought his season to a close. Thankfully he agreed to support the squad with one more competition and despite being clearly tired gained fourth in the A800 and third in the B 1500. Paskar Owor produced his usual clutch of points finishing third in the B800 and winning the B3000. Dan Mulhare too made a welcome return to the team and won the A3000 by just a whisker from a fast finishing Paskar. Both men had broken away from the field and battled each other over the last two laps. Dan finished with the bragging rights as previously he had also won the B1500. But it was the steeplechase that gladdened the eyes. New member Matthew Graham ran away from the field to win in impressive style. Matthew is just 22 years old and has a great future ahead. Will Cockerell again produced a solid effort for B race points despite his vertical drop with pike technique into the water. (Tom Daley eat your heart out!). Once again JC was our only representative in the 400H and also doubling up in the B110H. Gary Wilson produced another solid effort to get fourth in the A sprint hurdles. Belgrave were second ... Coming into the final relays Belgrave were second. But a makeshift sprint squad couldn't overcome a poor start while ten minutes later the long relay boys lined up to find they numbered but three. Someone had gone home unexpectedly. Fortunately Pierre Walker who had warmed down from the sprint relay had enough time to get his spikes back on and took over the final leg to gain the 6 points which ensured we finished equal third with Cardiff AC. This was the second match this year we had tied a place. Just one more point in each of these matches would have made a big difference to Belgrave's League standing . If ever proof was needed that "chasing for every extra point" remains the name of the game this was it. Harrow AC are doomed for the drop and Gateshead have only a slender chance of staying in Division 1. HHH on the other hand are going to experience the joys of next year’s Premiership. As a fellow SLAN club we wish them well. tributes-to-patricia-mead-2012: Patricia Anne Mead 1945-2010 " ... I was greatly shocked and upset. Pat was a lovely lady, loved by all, you could not have had a nicer person we will all have very fond memories of her. My big memory of Pat was when she very kindly drove me to hospital at Windsor after I had a bad fall at the British League. She was always ready to help. We will all miss her... " Gerry North v " ... Pat was an amazing woman and it was an honour to have known her ... " Phil Wicks, Captain (extended tribute on RunnersLife) v " ... we were so sorry to hear the sad news ... and that we won't see her happy, bubbling self armed with camera at Sutton Park again. ... first met Pat back in the early sixties when we trained together at Tooting Bec during the winter months. She was of course Selsonia then and I was with Wimbledon AC. Though we lost touch for many years , our paths eventually crossed again ... still following, or in Pat's case, working hard, with the sport we love ... " Christine and Eric Thompson, ex-Surrey AC v " ... really am lost for words, but ... shall remember her as a real breath of fresh air whenever we met on the track and at cross country. ... " Mick and Mavis Firth, South London Harriers v " ... we have known Pat for well over fifty years ... enjoyed a special relationship ... and will miss her a great deal. She supported our athletic endeavours and in more recent times has been an example of courage and fortitude ... " Marianne and Alan Black v " ... my trips to the UK were less frequent than I would have liked, any time I ran for the club it was the likes of ... Pat that made me feel back "at home" ... " Justin Chaston, Colorado, USA v " ... even when I left for Altrincham she would still shout me on during a race and have a chat afterwards .. " Simon Marwood, Altrincham & District AC v " ... I first met Pat almost 20 years ago when my son joined HHH, and I managed the YA team. In 2002 I took on organising the London Schools Track & Field championships and was so grateful for the help Pat gave as chief track judge at those championships every year until her illness, not only on the day but beforehand in recruiting other officials. Can't begin to get my thoughts together properly yet ... " Bridget Yule, member of Herne Hill Harriers and Commitee member, London Schools Athletics Association v " ... Have just returned ... to hear the sad, sad, news. We were both so upset ... " Charlie and Mary Dickinson v " ... Staff, volunteers and council members at England Athletics are very saddened to hear of the death of Pat Mead after her battle with illness. Pat was a great servant of the sport and, in particular, of Belgrave Harriers. Pat's was a friendly and ever enthusiastic face at events across the country and she will be sadly missed. ... " England Athletics v " ... when I first stepped inside the Belgrave tent how nervous I was as it was full of proper (!) runners and I thought wouldn't be anything like the small local running club I'd come from. How very wrong I was, everyone was welcoming .... [She] always remembered everything about everyone and always had time to ask how you were and how something was going about something you'd told her about weeks ago. She always made sure you had a piece of cake and any family member that you'd brought in with you had a cake and cuppa too. There was never a shortage of cake and tea and a slice and cup was always found who ever you were. If ever you left kit behind it would always be returned at your next meeting ... freshly washed and always smelt so fresh. We used to tease her about how much fabric conditioner she must have got through. ... " Liz Horrobin v " ... She made a great impression on so many people she came into contact with, and her friendliness, work ethic and competency will be greatly missed ... " Kevin Kelly (Herne Hill Harriers) v " ... I well remember her presence with us in Germany in 1964 and have watched her progress as athlete, official and administrator through to President ... She also gave great service to the AAA many years ago ... her work has already been sadly missed during her illness and the club will be greatly lacking by her absence in the years to come ..." Bill and Sheena Lucas v " ... will miss Patricia and remember the many hours we spent officiating at many meetings where her professionalism and light touch was much appreciated ... " John Gebbels (Herne Hill Harriers) v " ... Belgrave and the wider world have lost someone special ... " John and Heather Hall v " ... absolutely stunned ... When I think back to the 1960s I always remember the wonderful times ... It was like a light being switched on after years of austerity ... will always figure in my memories and certainly illuminated my life ... I can see her now, beautiful, lively and caring. Someone who I will always remember. ..." Chris Harvey (one time South London Harrier) v " ... My second mum ... " Jackie Bye (formerly Stone) v " ... A lovely, lively lady. We loved her and will miss her greatly ... " Eric and Mavis Hall v " ... I only have good memories of a happy smiling woman, normally with a camera round her neck, always positive and upbeat about all aspects in sport and life. ..." Tony Ganio v " ... I have very fond memories of Pat who was always so kind and thoughtful. Especially greeting us weary runners with a big smile and the hot cups of tea after some cold muddy cross country races! ... " Padraic Buckley and Trish v " ... Pat was an exceptional lady, who always made me feel welcome and part of the Belgrave family (yes - even after I defected to Cardiff!). The spirit, bonding and team atmosphere that she was able to create at events was very special. ... " Chris Moss (Cardiff AAC) v " ... a the truly wonderful person, Pat was so so , I'm stuck for word so I will just say Fantastic ... " Richard Partridge v " ... for some years, I could never bring myself to cease being a "Belle". I always have done and always will feel part of the ‘family’ and one of the reasons for this was the atmosphere engendered around the club, of whom [she] was one of the finest examples. She was always smiling (although sometime a little tensely during tight battles at relays!) always welcoming and always seemed genuinely interested. She was truly lovely ... " Juliette Clark v " ... I still remember her competing on the track when I last did – about 15 or so years ago and I can still picture her as being very young. ... " Jacinta Moore v " ... Her unselfish commitment to the sport has been amazing. During the late 1980's 90's and early 2000's I competed for Belgrave on many occasions and she was always there either "just helping out" or managing the team; enthusiasm and dedication from people such as Pat is what keeps the sport going... " Phil Carstairs v " ... I remember her as someone who was always happy and smiling, always positive and always willing to help out, a rare combination of attributes. ... May I personally and behalf of Surrey County AA offer my sympathy and condolences at this very sad time. Tom Pollak, Chairman, Surrey County Athletic Association v " ... There are many at the Thames Hare & Hounds who were so saddened to hear the news ... Pat was so much a part of Belgrave, and you two made a marvellous team and contributed wonderfully to what made the Belgrave-Thames rivalry so special for so many seasons. People like Pat are the engine-room of club athletics. She will be missed - not just by the Belgrave Harriers, but by many who valued her contribution to the grass-roots of our sport. ... " John Bryant, President, the Thames Hare & Hounds v " ... The road running section of our club has always felt like a family and along with yourselves, Pat can take the greatest amount of credit for this. From getting up at hours most of the boys couldn't imagine to put the tent up, to covering more miles supporting than most of us run, before providing such a dazzling array of post race cakes and then finally taking the tent down, Pat really made the big occasions special. Few can have given as much as she has to our sport and some of her achievements ... She was a truly exceptional person, who I will never forget. Richard Ward v " ... We have some great memories of Pat and these shall be with us for ever. Pat's hospitality and warm smile were second to none and will be much missed. She always made everybody feel so welcome and at ease in her company ... " Mark and Gemma Miles v " ... This is truly devastating news. From the day I joined Belgrave I was welcomed by your family, with Alan sorting winning teams and Hazel and Pat supplying the support and the cakes. It got to the stage where I still turned up for the 12 stage relay for one of Pat's cakes even when I was barely training and not doing any other racing (although with the extra pounds I was already carrying the last thing I needed was more cake!). The Mead family are what made me love road relays as much as I do and Pat is every bit a part of that love. She will be sadly missed but never forgotten. Let nobody doubt that Pat was a superstar and you and she were an example to us all. You should be very proud of the fact that your wife's (and mum's - Hazel) memory will always live on within the people who knew her ... " David Anderson v " ... Pat was held in the highest regard by all, as are the Mead family who many of us feel are the back bone of Belgrave Harriers. " Andy Lee-Gerrard (Herne Hill Harriers) v " ... Pat will be greatly missed not only by me, but by a good number of my Herne Hill Harriers clubmates ... " Geoff Jerwood (Herne Hill Harriers) v " ... she made an impact on me throughout the time I knew her. From day one she was friendly to me and always made sure I was ok. Pat's passing leaves a huge hole in the lives of all those who knew her, she was an inspiration and from a personal perspective the right kind of team manager - the kind of manager that people want to run their best for rather than for their own personal gain. I'm so glad I got to see her again at last year's Southern 6 stage and only sorry I won't get that chance again. ... I wasn't intending to run the National 6 stage but I've asked Geoff if he'll consider me for the team as I'd like to run in Pat's memory. Roger Alsop (Herne Hill Harriers) v " ... She will be sorely missed by so many people both in her role as an instrumental part of Belgrave ... and as a wonderful person as well. ... Pat always viewed the club as an extended family ... " Catherine Eastham v " ... Jane Everett [formerly Pritchard and one of the original three Belles] v " ... Paul, Lyn and Lauren Freary with kind thoughts also from Mike Freary and Rick Hayman v " .. Just feels so unfair that someone who was so full of life and did so much for so many is no longer with us. surrey-county-cross-country-championship: At last another Senior Men's team win in the 'Surreys' A thrilling race at Lloyd Park saw three Belgravians storming away on the first lap with a now healthy but far from racing fit Phil Wicks initially taking up his customary position in the lead. But Phil came up against a very fit Paskar Owor and the ever-strong James Kelly who gave him no quarter. On lap two the two leading Aldershot boys slowly worked their way nearer to the front and it was at that point that Paskar decided that some serious pace had to be injected to ensure an individual Belgrave win. With the leading group now blown apart Paskar cruised on for the win - the second time he has taken this title. The talented youngster Ian Bailey of AFD worked hard to pick up both James and Phil over the second half of the race but with three in the first four and backed up well by Will Cockerell and two guys who share over 100 years between them - Knut Hegvold and Mike Trees - we had 22 points in hand over a slowly strengthening Hercules Wimbledon and a slightly weaker than normal Herne Hill. It was our first County Cross team win since 1996 ... and before that 1967! It has been a long slow process working back towards the win with a series of: 1st, 3rd, dnf, dnf, 5th, dnf, 13th, dnf, dnf, 7th, 5th, 4th, 3rd, 3rd, 2nd, 2nd, and now 1st. Not a lover of the mud but well used to English conditions, James Kelly recently found muddy conditions much to his advantage in Spain when he beat European 34th placer and club mate Alberto Lozano de Pedro by a minute and a half. The Spaniards of course rarely see the stuff. Great credit to Phil Wicks, taking some tough hits for the team in these glutinous conditions. He's pleased to be back in a racing singlet once more - and we're delighted. Good luck to him in his comeback. 2xu-surrey-cc-league-division-one-race-3: Herpetologian horrors at Ham Lands Alan Mead reports:- In cold conditions alongside the River Thames the youngsters got under way half an hour earlier than normal, due to the failing light at this time of year, and within 20 minutes we were treated to the sight of Malik Nehaili coming home in third place in the under 13 group. Well done Malik! With several of our regular seniors suffering sickness it was going to be tight as to whether we would provide the requisite ten men to form a complete team. With five minutes to go we still only had eight – but then Donny, aiding Stragglers in hosting the race, suddenly pulled on his racing singlet and we had nine. There were some good class runners on display: our own Surrey County Champion Paskar Owor, Johnny Gilbert who won the Kent title from Andy Rayner and then previous Surrey winner Nick Torry (all running for Kent); there was guest Danny Davies from Aldershot and Middlesex Champion Chris Smith (running for Herne Hill). Yet again, though, it was Paskar holding sway and he really is building up a good sequence of runs. But the race wasn’t without drama. Running along the towpath next to the tidal section of the Thames was no joke. With the swollen river meeting the incoming tide on the first lap, the water was lapping over the river bank ankle deep. On the second circuit it was far worse, up to the knees … and by the time the tail-enders came through, the thighs. With the onset of global warming maybe we are going to have to consult the tide tables and state of the moon before setting start times for races at Ham Lands. Thank goodness the race started earlier than normal. Runners were somewhat shocked to have to wade through a hundred metres of this, not sure whether their next footfall in the murky flood-water would take them waist deep. Paskar, who apparently doesn’t swim, had the team in stitches in the after-race tall-tale competition, telling us to be thankful that this was an English river and not the Ugandan Kagera: "if this was Uganda there would be pythons in there!" In spite of the individual win the team placed a lowly 7th. Matt Taylor put in another strong performance to score 37th but Will had a real off-day, losing his shoe twice, and was under severe attack from our super 50s Mike Trees and Knut Hegvold. surrey-womens-cross-country-league-divis: Hanging on in there... Will Cockerell writes:- There was more tremendous fare on offer at this venue that was a regular in the 1980s but less seen of late. A sign that our squad is settled and focussed is to note our scoring five was identical to match 2. Their scoring spots barely changed either. This is a slight paradox in that consistency is a hallmark of good teams, but the TM is now concerned we are becoming too reliant on the fab five. What if something happens to one of them? Our back-up is sound but some way below that of our competitors. Indeed our B-team only lies 9th in the rankings, which is a bit shaky. Nothing for it - we've just got to keep building. And how churlish for the TM to say he wants more. Compare for instance this race to the one from exactly two years ago, Sammi was 8th - no change there then, Rieko was out to play again as well... but our points total after the 3 matches then was 980, and it's now 264. We've been without three big guns this year in Tilly, Catherine and Zoe - hopefully all will be back for '13-14. Yet again Ruth and Tish had a battle royale and their domination over the other 326 athletes is severe. They bring out the best of each other, and their upcoming clash at the South of England Championships in two weekend's time is to be savoured. Ruth has been making all the running of late, with Tish grimly trying to keep tabs. But she refused to let the elastic snap, and coming into the last 200 they were still inseparable. Another brutal slog for the line followed with Tish initially taking the lead, but in the last 60 metres Ruth clawed her back and inched her way to a splendid win - and her maiden Surrey League victory - many congratulations to her. Sam seemed to get better as the race wore on and we all hope she has a similar resounding performance in the Southerns as she produced on that famous day last year. Fee had a self-confessed shocker at the counties ("only 8th" - greedy girl!), but felt much better here, while Jojo has had time-out, but it's now blinkers on and she intends to get better with every race between now and April. Anne yet again under-pinned us with steely fortitude. Our back-up today came from the Vixster, great to see her commuting in for the Belles for the second week running, and she's running well at the mo, back into the top 25% of fields where she belongs. Rieko was dependable as ever, and we're always delighted to see another debutante, and in this case it was Maisie-Rose Byrne, who runs with a nonchalant demeanour and dispatched 180 bodies in the combined race. In the team stakes it was a thriller, as Thames flirted with 4th, finishing just ahead of a quickly improving Herne Hill, but the Belles saw both of them off while Dulwich were outstanding, and come back into the overall reckoning. For now it's still Thames's to lose but we can have done no more than we have, to go into the last race 2-1 up on them for the three races. Some years ago this is how they scored it in the Surrey League, merely counting where the club finished on the day. ie. 1st scored 15, and 15th 1. We would be in the lead if they still did that, but this way is undoubtedly fairer and means that every position is scrapped for and meaningful. 2xu-surrey-cc-league-division-one-race-4: Paskar the individual league champion - but Bels must beware complacency next season Alan Mead reports:- It was a bleak day on Farthing Downs for the last league race of the 2012-2013 series. Frank Tickner stormed away from the start as if to tell Paskar that there was no way he was going to beat him again. No doubt Mr Tickner is rounding into the sort of form that he likes to be in as the Southern and National approach. It seemed Paskar was a little out of sorts as he also had to give way to two more Kent men as they swamped the front part of the field to win the day ... and leapfrog Thames to take the league title in their first year in the division. In fact they were unable to score Nick Torry, in 3rd, as they were over their quota of second-claimers. Nevertheless, Paskar had no trouble in holding on to his individual title ... yet again. It's a sobering thought that if we didn't have our Ugandan ace fighting our corner we would have been be very, very close to being relegated this winter. Another good contribution came from Matt Taylor and John Needham, in his first race for the Bels was into the scoring ten. Ranelagh had made a great effort to turn out a strong final squad and as a result pushed the Bels down to 5th on the day ... and 6th in the league. We are going to have to watch things carefully next season if we are to keep clear of the relegation zone. On hand to watch the race was Alan Black, the winner of the final race of the '62-'63 season - held on exactly the same day - 9 February - 50 years ago. Where does the time go? Your chronicler remembers it as if it was yesterday - over at muddy Addington. For some inexplicable reason young Malik Nehaili - an Under 13 - has been included in the Under 17 results. We'll get this sorted because his 18:13 would have placed him fourth in his correct age group. surrey-womens-cross-country-league-divis: Engine Room Swings Into Gear Will Cockerell reports:- This was a gung-ho tribe that rounded off our campaign and we were pleased to welcome two new names to our all-time list of Surrey League scorers. After that incredible start by Thames back in October, the league title always seemed just out of reach, and after sniffing about the possibility of dragging Sammi and Tish to the course in shackles [they ran 78 and 79 at Wokingham], and parachuting in Lou from Cheshire, we still felt it wouldn't have quite been enough. Maybe we could have scored 55 points and hope for a miracle? We'd still have been 3 pips short! So instead this was a day for our engine-room to come to the party - the backbone and foundation of any successful club - and they excelled themselves. After Fee's metronomic sequence of finishes for the season of 16, 18, 21 & 19, Jojo turned in another peach, whilst Vix is flying at the mo, up from 58th to 45th on a month ago. Laura had even more of a stunner and turned her Nonsuch 90th into 58th, while Maisie's 101 on debut is now 88th. Finally, welcome to Belgrave 'Run and Become' employee Petra Kasperova. Petra kept tabs on Laura all through to indicate she will be a useful ally in the years to come. It was exciting to watch Dulwich's assault on Thames for the title. It was touch and go, and a clerical error initially awarded the spoils the Dulwich, but instead it was Thames who claimed the trophy by a mere 17 points. How well we did to scalp them in two out of four events, and we look forward to another exciting scrap next season. With Herne Hill and West 4 also on the rise, and SLH always solid, it could be a six-way battle for supremacy. Many thanks to the 16 runners who fought so hard for us this term - 3rd place in such a strong league is honourable. seaa-cc-champs-parliament-hill-fields-20: "Little dog!" Alan Mead writes:- Starting half-way up the hill instead of down at the Lido was a slight relief but there was still 50 minutes of running ahead of our stalwarts who come together each year to celebrate the toughest cross country race in our calendar. The postponement from three weeks earlier, due to the Heath being snowbound, resulted in a few of our men being unable to turn out; overall the field was down about 40% but the team race was hit hard. Paskar and Andrew Connick were both prominent as the field went over the top and round the back of Kite Hill for the first time but already it was Frank Tickner of Wells City and Bedford’s Neilson Hall slugging it out for the lead. A lap later, with both our men in the ‘teens and the mud spattering up to eye level, it was Andrew putting our Vice-Captain under a pressure he hasn’t faced all winter – a club-mate showing every sign of getting away from him. Will Cockerell and Matt Taylor (what a boost he has given our team this winter) were similarly locked together and with Mike Trees and Roy Maddams completing the six and John Needham and Tom Hadfield backing up, we showed every sign of finishing a squad in a reasonable position. Bedford & County had the team race stitched up by a long way. As Mike headed out again he was overtaken by a barking pooch that was having the time of his life. Following the flags over hill and dale he cheerfully barked and looked up at every runner he overtook with a sort of doggy grin: “Come on, hang on to me, we can catch ‘em.” Eight or nine minutes later our friend had worked his way further up the field, still going well, and as the racers came towards the end of lap two he’d caught Will and was by now drawing as much support as the runners: “Come on Will, come on Matt, come on dog!” Our own team manager was all for slipping a Belgrave vest on him but the course police arrested said canine, now intent on making an assault on the leaders, before he could set out on lap three. Stitch caused Andrew a few problems over the second half of the race but his was a brilliant run. What a way to celebrate his birthday. Paskar was less than happy in the mud and Matt Taylor eventually got the better of the Cockerpillar. They don’t come any tougher than Mike Trees – an M50 and having just driven down from Northumberland to race, was going back again that night – what a hero. Sixth as a squad was not bad at all. And our headline? An expression used by H.G.Wells’ Mr Polly whenever he found himself in a sticky situation and similarly used by your correspondent on occasions when a swift exit has been required. ecca-national-cc-championships-herringto: The National's Glorious Ebb and Flow Will Cockerell writes: - The Belles' 2012-13 cross-country campaign ended with this interesting little scamper under the Penshaw Monument folly. To the uninitiated, there was plenty more folly going on down below, but for some reason, the craziness of the day makes sense to a good portion of the 3,000+ participants, as much as paint-balling, cheese-rolling or dwarf tossing does to others. To be sure, the logistics don't seem to jive. A 16-17-hour round trip for 30-40 minutes of the most gluey, gloopy, freezing, ghoulish conditions one ever did see. 2007 this was not, when Frank Tickner shimmied round the park in 37:31. Keith Gerrard needed more than 30-seconds-per-mile to take care of the distance - and this correspondent 41. At around 0630hrs Sammi, Tish & Ma, Laura, Hester and the 'pillar popped their heads out from their burrows, and started out on the fiddly journey to King's Cross. Loading up on caffeine, they were then smoothly ferried up to Sunderland grimly noting that England's green and pleasant land started to turn white at around York (aided and abetted by a snowstorm). They were greeted at Sunderland by the aptly named Lou Blizzard, a key scorer in the best National performance in our history in 2005 [12th]. A seven-seater cab whisked us up to Herrington (and how nice to see the park's namesake, Chaz, in the crowd - our 15th most 'blinged' relay-runner this century and key National cross man in our Stowe and Bristol campaigns of 2000 and '02). It didn't take much to see that the battlefield before us was not for the faint-hearted. Mud splattered athletes from the age-groups walked around like zombies, long since having lost feeling in their extremities. Half-an-hour before the gun and SA's feet were frozen blocks which given her other niggles was always going to make running at optimum pace a problem. For a moment there was concern that she would DNS, but announced: "I haven't come all this way for nothing." A final photo op with JK before the off, who was pastiche-interviewed about the Belles' prospects: "Think this lot can go top 6, Jim?" "Well looking at them they seem very mean, lean and hungry, so they must have a chance." Profound. Early doors and it was clear Lou had a big problem. She had stepped in a hole the week before and her ankle had blown up to twice the size. Surely the National was out, but she wouldn't let it go, and after nailing the Wrexham Half declared herself fit. But suspect ankles were like a match to a scarecrow on this course, and Lou was in for a whole world of pain. That she stuck it out was a marvel - a true Belgrave hero. But we had back-up, and Jojo was suddenly under the spotlight, and didn't she grab it with glee, nearly scoring 2nd for us as it went, as she placed Fee behind her for the first time. Fee was 17 pips up on her excellent National of last year, and yet again was the backbone of our operation. We are so grateful to the 'Maycock massive' for all the support they've given us these last two years, and particular menche should go to Drew and Finlay, who are uncomplaining, often hypothermic, and on this occasion clad in footwear more appropriate for Ibiza. Laura had a cracker to go way inside the top half, whilst our 'sweeper' HBR bashed out the 'stat' of the day, as she turned her 302 last year into 145. Which only leaves our 'two-headed monster', who have catapulted us into the limelight this season. Sam toiled in the gloop and never gave up, and the roads will feel so easy after this. We know given fairer conditions this is a very fine cross-country runner - Brighton '12 - proved that, but this was about getting the job done, when she could instead have imploded. If we thought Tish was exceptional last week, this was truly stunning. Her 1:35 defeat to Steph Twell in London became a mere 12 seconds here, as it just shows that no-one, no matter their class and experience, was exempt from turmoil if things started to go awry. As for Tish, despite struggling to control her nerves, she executed her race dead centre, and typically for her, still craved more. That 'more' will come race-by-race, as she is steadily climbs up the ranks of England's foremost endurance runners. So, scores at the doors? We got that top 6, with the next three clubs neatly lined up bang in front of us - ooh, what could have been with a bit more luck. But they'll all say the same - Hallamshire for instance lost Hattie Dean the week before - so no ifs, no buts, this is where we currently belong in the nation's pecking order. Some logistical acrobatics were required, but well worth all the effort and expense. This team is perfectly poised for many more top-sixes over the coming generation - bring it on. A magnificent 25th place came from James Kelly in the men's race. "I died a thousand deaths over the last kilometre," he later admitted, "Bring on the 12 stage." Sadly we were unable to get a full team together and as a result several of those who had planned to run baulked at a round trip of 600 miles to run in an incomplete team. Malik Nehaili showed his love of the sport by combining a run in the under 13 Boys event while on a few days break in the North East. erra-womens-national-6-stage-road-relay-: Belles just out of the medals President and Team Manager Charlie Dickinson, Rose O'Brien, Tish Jones, Jo Rhodes, Fee Maycock, Alison Heydenrych, Sam Amend, Louise Blizzard and Vikki Goodwin. Charlie Dickinson writes:- A very strong team came to Sutton Park with just a hope of getting one of the minor South of England medals, given out because of the Milton Keynes cancellation three weeks ago. After a wonderful performance from everyone, the team were left disappointed just 12 seconds short of the bronze. What a wonderful group of girls we have, the Magnificent 8. All arrived early, warmed up themselves without being reminded, reported to the changeover in good time, supported and encouraged each other, and ran their hearts out, a Team Manager’s Dream! Jojo ran the first leg to order. Not phased by the fast mass start and top loading teams, she kept to her own pace finishing strongly just as predicted. Rose on leg two, a 400m track girl, but with an excellent ‘Bridges’ a week ago, kept to a sensible steady pace up to the memorial, but just as she was set to unleash that track speed down the hill, she was crippled with severe stitch and had to ease off right at the wrong time. She still finished strongly to complete in a very satisfactory time but was left very frustrated hoping low 18's. Louise has been troubled by a badly swollen ankle and worried that she would let the team down after missing a great deal of training. She did nothing of the sort running a typically gutsy third leg pulling back three places. Then to Tish on leg 4. She ran just as we have come to expect from our new superstar. Flying round in 16:51 she moved us up from 27th to 14th and getting just about in sight of those medals. Sammi on the difficult leg five has herself been nursing and ignoring her Achilles injury prior to the marathon next week. We can always count on Sammi to pull out a great performance and this was no exception. With large gaps to chase down she moved us up one more place to 13th. The always dependable Fee was trusted with the final leg and she ran a blinder and in now difficult windy conditions a mere one second from her time last year. Storming past the girl from Norwich just 30 meters from the finish was typical of how she has run all season. Then the long wait for the results, were the South not giving the silver to Aldershot ‘B’ whose ‘A’ team had got the gold miles in front? We were ahead of Norwich, did that make us third? But no, we had overlooked the runner from Bedford running 17.35 on the last leg to pip us by an agonising 12 seconds. If only! The stitch, the ankle, the Achilles, all finding just another two seconds each! But that's how we all are, never happy always wanting more, and all determined to come back next year and get that medal! But we were not done yet, up to the top of the hill to egg on the men's team and to see our Will stick to the Leeds man like glue and not let him get away. And so pleased for him to get that gold medal after all he has done for the women's team. A final huge thank you to Vicky and Alison who came as reserves, never complained and were truly just as much part of the team. Alison ran a blinder on leg two and showed that if it had been seven legs we would have certainly got that medal! southern-athletics-league-division-3-s-m: Not a bad turn-out in sunny if somewhat windy conditions. A happy band had travelled down in the mini-bus driven by Don Anderson but Triathlon superstar Richard Stannard cycled the 70 miles to Hastings to run in the 5000m. That race was won by Matt Graham who was unchallenged after throwing in a 69 second first lap. Not a single point was dropped in the men's throws - great work by Chris Privett and Pete Mayfield. 800 metre winner James Myatt found out that he could triple jump by handsomely winning that event and also enjoyed himself by tackling the high jump, 1500m and 4x400m where he looked every inch a one lap racer. Biggest points scorer for Belgrave among the women's events was hammer thrower Rachel Basford who won that and took in the other throws, long jump and hurdles before finishing off with the relays. Team Manager Hazel Mead made it a hammer double by winning the B event in a near personal best. Jessica Case won the B 400 hurdles while Rose O'Brien and Sandra Dike seemed to pop up all over the arena. With a few more of those blank spaces on the team sheet filled we can start challenging for a team win. Nice to see Bob Bridges back with the team.
